result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers pick the same direction: a 50-page capped trial, a sandbox and a repriced starter plan. Both get the per-page arithmetic right, but neither gives the full $20,000 worst case. B wins because it names a practical abuse risk, people opening multiple accounts to get more pages, and gives fixes (email verification, IP and disposable-email limits, optional card). A never mentions abuse, though it is better on what to watch, because it ties adjusting the offer to whether credit users go on to pay. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers drop the forever-free tier, propose a 50-page cap and a sandbox, and correctly find that $10 for 500 pages leaves no margin. Neither gives the roughly $20,000/month worst case. A wins because it names the abuse risk of repeat signups and gives concrete fixes (email verification, IP and disposable-email limits, a card requirement as a fallback). B says nothing about abuse. B does name a better metric to watch, the share of credit users who convert to paid, while A only tracks first-session page usage.
